title: HiBREW Espresso Machines Compared: H10 Plus vs H13 vs H7 Lite vs H7A
metaDescription: HiBREW espresso machine lineup compared: H10 Plus (entry semi-auto), H13 (machine + grinder bundle), H7 Lite (all-in-one with grinder), and H7A (dual boiler, 30 grind levels) — which setup fits your counter and your coffee habit.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: HiBREW's espresso lineup looks like four versions of the same machine until you check what's actually included in the box — one is just the espresso maker, one bundles a separate grinder, one has the grinder built in, and one adds a dual boiler with 30 grind levels. That difference, not the 20-bar pressure figure they all share, is what decides which one makes sense for your counter space and how much work you're willing to do per shot. Here's what actually separates them.

items.label: H10 Plus — What's Included
items.value: Espresso machine only, 20 bar, fast heating — you supply your own grinder

items.label: H13 — What's Included
items.value: Semi-automatic espresso machine + G5 coffee grinder as a bundle — two separate units

items.label: H7 Lite — What's Included
items.value: Espresso maker with an integrated grinder, 20 bar, 1350W — one unit, grinder built in

items.label: H7A — What's Included
items.value: 20 bar, dual boiler system, 30 grind levels — the most capable model in the lineup

items.label: Pressure
items.value: 20 bar across all four — the shared baseline, not the differentiator

items.label: Grinder
items.value: The main split: no grinder (H10 Plus) vs. bundled separate grinder (H13) vs. built-in grinder (H7 Lite, H7A)

pros: All four hit 20 bar pressure, which is the standard for proper espresso extraction — you're not downgrading pressure by buying the cheaper model
The H7 Lite and H7A combine grinder and brewer in one unit, saving real counter space versus a separate grinder setup
The H13 bundle pairs the machine with a dedicated G5 grinder — a burr-style separate grinder usually grinds more consistently than a built-in one at the same price
The H7A's dual boiler system means you can brew and steam milk simultaneously rather than waiting between steps — a real workflow upgrade, not a spec-sheet number
30 grind levels on the H7A gives noticeably more dial-in range for different beans and brew styles than simpler grinders
cons: The H10 Plus has no grinder at all — budget for a separate one, or you're stuck with pre-ground coffee and noticeably worse shots
Built-in grinders (H7 Lite, H7A) are convenient but harder to upgrade or replace later than a standalone grinder
Semi-automatic machines still require you to dose, tamp, and time the shot yourself — none of these are push-button automatic
The H7A's dual boiler and higher price only pay off if you regularly make milk drinks — for straight espresso, the extra cost buys less than it sounds

items.question: Which HiBREW espresso machine should I buy?
items.answer: If you already own a grinder or want to choose your own separately, the H10 Plus covers the brewing side at the lowest price. If you want a proper separate burr grinder and machine in one purchase, the H13 bundle is the pick. If counter space matters and you'd rather have one unit, the H7 Lite's built-in grinder covers that. If you regularly make milk drinks and want the widest grind range, the H7A's dual boiler and 30 grind levels are worth the step up.

items.question: Is a dual boiler espresso machine worth it over a single boiler?
items.answer: It comes down to whether you make milk drinks regularly. A dual boiler lets you brew espresso and steam milk at the same time instead of waiting for the machine to switch between the two — a real time-saver when making multiple cappuccinos or lattes back to back. For straight espresso or occasional milk drinks, a single boiler handles it fine, and the H7A's extra cost is harder to justify.

items.question: Do I need a grinder, or can I use pre-ground coffee?
items.answer: Technically you can use pre-ground coffee, but the shots will be noticeably worse — espresso is very sensitive to grind freshness and fineness, and pre-ground coffee goes stale within days of opening. If you're buying an espresso machine at all, a grinder (standalone like the H13's G5, or built-in like the H7 Lite and H7A) is the difference between mediocre and genuinely good shots. The H10 Plus assumes you already have one or will buy one.

items.question: What does 20 bar pressure actually mean on an espresso machine?
items.answer: It's the pump's rated maximum pressure, and 20 bar is now standard across this class. The important detail is that proper espresso extraction happens around 9 bar at the group head — the higher pump rating is headroom for maintaining consistent pressure, not a sign that more pressure makes better coffee. All four HiBREW models share the same 20 bar rating, so it's not what separates them; the grinder situation and boiler design are.

sections.content: The 20 bar pressure number is identical across all four — what you're actually choosing between is how the grinder is handled and whether you want a dual boiler. H10 Plus if you already have a grinder, H13 if you want one bundled separately, H7 Lite if you want everything in one unit, H7A if you make milk drinks regularly and want the widest grind range. Pick based on your counter space and how many milk drinks you actually make, not the pressure figure every model shares.
